filename: Pushing the frontiers in climate modelling and analysis with machine learning.pdf
title: Pushing the frontiers in climate modelling and analysis with machine learning
processes: ocean mesoscale eddies and momentum forcing
ocean heat uptake and tracer transport
parameterization_target: Subgrid-scale atmospheric convection, clouds, gravity wave drag, ocean mesoscale eddy closures, and terrestrial ecosystem flux regulation
code_availability: Several open source code repositories and workflows are referenced, including NVIDIA Modulus-Makani (https://github.com/NVIDIA/modulus-makani), AI2 ACE (https://github.com/ai2cm/ace), and ESMValTool (https://esmvaltool.org).
testbed_rationale: This paper is a Perspective/review article setting forth research directions, challenges, and opportunities in ML for Earth system modelling; it does not produce or host new standalone datasets.
pain_points: Disparities between offline accuracy and online coupled simulation stability and skill
Poor out-of-distribution generalization to warmer unseen climate states
Violation of physical conservation laws (energy, mass, momentum)
Instabilities arising from nonlinear coupling between ML subgrid parameterizations and resolved dynamical cores
Quantifying uncertainty across both stochastic (aleatoric) and structural/epistemic sources
Explainability and physical interpretation of deep learning black-box predictions
Causal inference challenges under non-stationarity, cyclic feedbacks, and hidden confounding
extraction_notes: Perspective article published in Nature Climate Change reviewing the state of ML in Earth system modelling, highlighting hybrid physics-ML models, emulation, extremes detection/attribution, model evaluation/benchmarking, and cross-cutting challenges (generalizability, UQ, XAI, causality).
